prompt:
You receive 4 images. Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Repaint image 1 into a finished painting: keep every line and every block exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, paint each block as the object described below, do not move, enlarge, shrink, add or remove anything, and leave no flat colour areas or hard geometric edges. Images 2-3 are photos of the real place (geography, architecture, materials and real details to paint from; they are references only, do not copy their camera, cars, people, signs or weather). Image 4 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the local shopping centre at Triangel / Monar in Čierna Voda (municipality Chorvátsky Grob, near Bratislava, Slovakia). Images 2-3 are dashcam photos of this real place: a long single-storey wing with salmon-pink render, a green metal roof and tall narrow windows, standing above a grass bank by the road (image 2, left), and the two-storey end of the same centre with salmon render, green roofs and bronze-framed glazing (image 3, left). Paint the facade of one small invented grocery shop in this salmon wing - not any of the real businesses there.

Brief: a small invented grocery shop selling through its service window during the pandemic: the shop is closed for customers, the shop assistant serves through the window behind glass; a plastic crate on a table outside; hand-drawn price cards without any brands. Thursday 29 October 2020, a sunny autumn afternoon around half past three: warm low sunlight from the left falling across the facade, soft shadows to the right, an autumn tree beyond the corner of the building, a few fallen leaves on the pavement.

Camera: eye-level, straight-on view of the shop facade; vertical lines stay vertical. The facade meets the pavement along one straight horizontal line at y 780 across the whole width. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch: the green metal roof edge along the top edge (y 0-50), the tops of the tall bronze-framed shop windows at y 128, the window sills at y 600-614, the dark grey plinth y 700-780, the pavement from y 780 down to the bottom edge.

What the sketch blocks are, left to right: a tall display window with shelves of unbranded groceries inside (bread, jars, vegetables, bottles with plain labels); the tall service window, whose lower sash is slid open as a service hatch behind a clear plexiglass screen with a small gap at the bottom, a narrow counter ledge at its sill (top edge at y 602) and the dim, empty shop interior with shelves behind; next to the hatch a small wooden folding table with a blue plastic crate of groceries and a bottle of hand sanitiser; the closed glass entrance door with a paper notice taped inside (illegible scribbles); a second tall shop window with shelves and two faded posters (illegible); the corner of the building; beyond it an autumn tree, grass and a piece of blue sky. Plain salmon render above the windows, no sign.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 120-240, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (6-12 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): a big hand-written cardboard price card taped inside the upper pane of the left display window, with a hand-drawn potato and big hand-written round price numbers in red marker (no words, no brand).
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 425-545, y 150-250 of the 1920x1080 frame (22-28 % from the left, 14-23 % from the top): in the upper glazing of the service window, on a display shelf just behind the glass, a wooden crate heaped with potatoes, a few of them sprouting.

Walkable floor: the band at x 90-1830, y 790-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (5-95 % from the left, 73-94 % from the top) is the open pavement of grey concrete tiles - one continuous flat surface with no kerb, no step, no edge and no change of material inside it, and nothing standing on it: no tables, no crates, no bins, no plants, no signs, no bags. Only light, soft shadows and a few fallen leaves. The pavement continues to the left edge (the area of the layout sketch at x 50-105, y 975-1045 of the 1920x1080 frame (3-5 % from the left, 90-97 % from the top)).
NPC zone at x 385-535, y 450-770 of the 1920x1080 frame (20-28 % from the left, 42-71 % from the top): an animated character sprite will stand here later, so paint only plain, uncluttered background in it - no person, no figure, no silhouette, no clothes on hooks that read as a person. The upper part of this zone is the service-hatch opening above the counter ledge: paint it as the dim, empty shop interior behind clear plexiglass; below the ledge it is plain wall and plinth.

Fiction rules: the shop, its name and the assistant are invented: no shop name, no logos, no brands on goods, posters or parasols, no real business signage from the photos; prices hand-drawn, without brands. No people, no animals.

The layout sketch is a blocking aid only: paint over all of it. Do NOT draw frames, borders, outlines or boxes around objects, and keep no flat colour block. The finished picture contains no UI, no captions, no text except what is asked for above, no watermark and no people or animals.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
